```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

This vignette recomputes the decision-churn numbers in section 2 of
`docs/STATUS.md` from the frozen Louisiana fixture, and stops with an error if
any of them differs from the committed results manifest
(`analysis/louisiana/results/EXPECTED-RESULTS.json`,
`monte_carlo$decisions_replicate`). The full analysis also reports interval
widths, subgroup associations and the equalisation experiment; those stay in
`analysis/` and are not reproduced here.

## Inputs

The fixture holds the 19 count-level components behind the 16 SVI 2022
variables for the 1,379 tracts CDC publishes, as the point estimate plus the 80
ACS variance replicates. Its provenance is recorded in
`tests/testthat/test-louisiana.R`.

```{r inputs}
library(svichurn)
cx <- readRDS("../tests/testthat/fixtures/la_counts.rds")
dim(cx$NUM)
table(cx$comp_var)[c("SNGPNT", "MUNIT", "CROWD")]   # the two-component variables
```

## The composite specification

SVI 2022 is sixteen variables in four themes, each percentile-ranked, summed
with unit weights within a theme, summed across themes, and percentile-ranked
again. Writing it out is all it takes to point the function at a different
index: change the variable list, the grouping, the weights or the threshold.

```{r spec}
svi_2022 <- list(
  comp_var  = cx$comp_var,
  themes    = list(
    theme1 = c("POV150", "UNEMP", "HBURD", "NOHSDP", "UNINSUR"),
    theme2 = c("AGE65", "AGE17", "DISABL", "SNGPNT", "LIMENG"),
    theme3 = c("MINRTY"),
    theme4 = c("MUNIT", "MOBILE", "CROWD", "NOVEH", "GROUPQ")),
  aggregate = "rank",
  threshold = c(0.90, 0.80, 0.75)        # top decile, quintile, quartile
)
```

## Churn at B = 5,000

The seed and RNG kind are those of `05_replicate_simulation.R`, whose first
design is the one `composite_churn()` runs, so the draws are the same draws.

```{r churn}
RNGkind("Mersenne-Twister", "Inversion", "Rejection")
set.seed(20260818)
out <- composite_churn(cx$NUM, cx$DEN, svi_2022, B = 5000)
ch <- attr(out, "churn")
ch
```

Leavers and entrants are reported separately. Their sum is the symmetric
difference between the published and the resampled funded sets; dividing it by
the number funded double-counts every replacement and roughly doubles the
churn rate. That error was made once in this project and withdrawn.

```{r decile}
d <- out[out$threshold == 0.90, ]
c(funded_p_lt_090   = sum(d$funded0 & d$p_funded < 0.90),
  unfunded_p_gt_010 = sum(!d$funded0 & d$p_funded > 0.10))
```

## Check against the manifest

```{r check}
manifest <- data.frame(   # EXPECTED-RESULTS.json, monte_carlo$decisions_replicate
  threshold              = c(0.90, 0.80, 0.75),
  n_funded               = c(137, 273, 342),
  expected_leavers       = c(34.17352001, 51.21307818, 54.38169452),
  leaver_rate            = c(0.24944175, 0.18759369, 0.1590108),
  expected_entrants      = c(34.17896349, 51.2238778, 54.1436516),
  expected_label_changes = c(68.3524835, 102.43695598, 108.52534612))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(round(ch, 8), manifest, check.attributes = FALSE,
                           tolerance = 0)),
          sum(d$funded0 & d$p_funded < 0.90) == 99,
          sum(!d$funded0 & d$p_funded > 0.10) == 120)
```

Every value agrees with the manifest to the eight decimals it records. In
words: of the 137 tracts in Louisiana's published top decile, an expected
34.2 (24.9%) would not be on the list if the survey were drawn again, and
34.2 others would take their place. The leaver rate is 18.8% for the top
quintile and 15.9% for the top quartile. All of these are descriptive
statements about one state and one edition of the index.
